func classifyToolType(name string) string {
	writeTools := map[string]bool{
		"write_file": true, "edit_file": true, "apply_patch": true,
	}
	readTools := map[string]bool{
		"read_file": true, "list_dir": true, "retrieve_tool_result": true,
	}
	searchTools := map[string]bool{
		"grep_files": true, "file_search": true, "web_search": true,
		"fetch_url": true,
	}
	shellTools := map[string]bool{
		"exec_shell": true, "task_shell_start": true, "task_shell_wait": true,
		"exec_shell_wait": true, "exec_interact": true, "exec_shell_interact": true,
	}
	taskTools := map[string]bool{
		"update_plan": true, "todo_write": true, "checklist_write": true,
		"task_create": true, "task_read": true, "task_list": true,
	}

	if writeTools[name] {
		return schema.ToolTypeWrite
	}
	if readTools[name] {
		return schema.ToolTypeRead
	}
	if searchTools[name] {
		return schema.ToolTypeSearch
	}
	if shellTools[name] {
		return schema.ToolTypeShell
	}
	if taskTools[name] {
		return schema.ToolTypeTask
	}

	return schema.ToolTypeGeneric
}

147	// waitFor polls until *counter reaches want or the test times out, accounting
148	// for the watcher dispatching callbacks on a goroutine.
149	func waitFor(t *testing.T, mu *sync.Mutex, counter *int, want int) {
150		t.Helper()
151		for i := 0; i < 200; i++ {
152			mu.Lock()
153			got := *counter
154			mu.Unlock()
155			if got == want {
156				return
157			}
158			if got > want {
159				t.Fatalf("callback fired %d times, want %d", got, want)
160			}
161			time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
162		}
163		t.Fatalf("callback never reached %d", want)
164	}

### 3.5 Tool catalog (real args observed)

| tool `name` | exact `args` keys (excl. `toolAction`/`toolSummary`) | result step `type` | result content shape | SpecStory tool type |

| `view_file` | `AbsolutePath` (str) | `VIEW_FILE` | `File Path:` + `Total Lines`/`Total Bytes` + line-numbered body (`N: <line>`) | **read** |
| `write_to_file` | `CodeContent` (str, full file body), `Description` (str), `IsArtifact` (bool), `Overwrite` (bool), `TargetFile` (str abs path) | `CODE_ACTION` | `Created file file://... with requested content.` | **write** |
| `replace_file_content` | `TargetFile` (str), `TargetContent` (str, old text), `ReplacementContent` (str, new text), `StartLine` (int), `EndLine` (int), `Instruction` (str), `Description` (str), `AllowMultiple` (bool) | `CODE_ACTION` | `The following changes were made by the replace_file_content tool to: <path>` + unified diff between `[diff_block_start]`/`[diff_block_end]` markers | **write** (edit) |
| `grep_search` | `Query` (str), `SearchPath` (str), `MatchPerLine` (bool) | `GREP_SEARCH` | JSON-lines, one per match: `{"File":...,"LineNumber":N,"LineContent":...}` | **search** |
| `list_dir` | `DirectoryPath` (str) | `LIST_DIRECTORY` | JSON-lines per entry `{"name":...,"isDir":true}` or `{"name":...,"sizeBytes":"NN"}`, then `Summary: This directory contains X subdirectories and Y files.` (or `Empty directory`) | **read** |

Tools NOT exercised in capture but likely to exist (the planner referred to its
"search tool"/"file viewer" by capability, and the CLI has a sandbox/browser
subsystem): `codebase_search` (semantic search), browser/URL tools
(`execute_url`/`read_url` appear in `list_permissions` output), MCP tools
(`mcp(*)` permission), subagent/task tools. A parser should treat any unknown
tool `name` as **generic** and map by `type` of the following result step.

### 3.6 `transcript.jsonl` double-escaping (the difference)
Same step at step_index 7 (`write_to_file`), both files:

`transcript_full.jsonl` (native — USE THIS):
```json
{"CodeContent":"hi there\n","IsArtifact":false,"Overwrite":true,"TargetFile":"/tmp/.../greeting.txt", ...}
```
`transcript.jsonl` (each value re-stringified — booleans/ints become strings):
```json
{"CodeContent":"\"hi there\\n\"","IsArtifact":"false","Overwrite":"true","TargetFile":"\"/tmp/.../greeting.txt\"", ...}
```
Rule for `transcript.jsonl`: after parsing the line, each `args` value is itself
a JSON-encoded scalar — decode a second time (string→string, `"false"`→bool,

---

## `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go`

**Lines 13, 91-94 (new): Registers the provider under id `antigravity`**

- (1) ✅ Follows the existing registration pattern exactly (construct → map → debug log).
- (2) ⚠️ The id string `"antigravity"` is a literal here while `provider.go:19` defines `const providerID = "antigravity"` for analytics. Two sources of truth for the same id — the const isn't exported so the registry can't use it, but that's the same drift every sibling provider has.

---

## `pkg/config/config.go`

**Lines 136-137, 246-253, 971-972 (new): `antigravity_cmd` config key**

- (3) ✅ Correct three-part change: template comment, struct field, `GetProviderCmd` case. Nothing missed.
- (4) ✅ Gofmt realigned the struct tags — noise, but unavoidable.
- (5) ✅ Good catch updating the `GetProviderCmd` doc comment to also list `deepseek`, which was previously missing.

---

## `pkg/cmd/session_tui_view.go`

**Lines 402-420 (new): `agentColWidth()` + padded `agentTag`**

- (6) ✅ Real problem, correctly diagnosed: `"antigravity"` is 11 chars and `%-8s` would shove every following column right on that row only.
- (7) ✅ Excellent "why" comment — explains both the widening and *why the floor of 8 exists* (preserves prior layout).
- (8) ⚠️ `m.agentColWidth()` iterates the `m.agents` map on every call, and it's called 1–2× per rendered row per frame. Trivial cost, but it's a constant for the lifetime of the model — computing it once when `m.agents` is populated would be simpler to reason about *and* cheaper.
- (9) ⚠️ The magic number `8` now appears in four places (`agentColWidth`'s floor, and `- 8` at `session_tui_view.go:198`, `:217`, `session_tui_browser.go:917`). A `const agentColMinWidth = 8` would make the relationship explicit; right now a reader has to infer that the `- 8` subtractions are undoing the same floor.
- (10) ✅ Line 215-217's comment ("A longer agent column … shrink the label budget to match") is exactly the kind of why-comment the codebase asks for.

## `pkg/cmd/session_tui_browser.go`

**Lines 251-268 (modified): `colorForAgent` palette**

- (11) ✅ Adding `case "antigravity"` is required by the PR.
- (12) ✅ Adding `"cursoride"` to the cursor case fixes a real pre-existing gap (cursoride rows had no accent).
- (13) ❓ Every *other* agent's color also changed (claude 170→terracotta, codex 42→#219B75, gemini, droid, deepseek). That's a palette rebrand riding along in a provider PR. Harmless and arguably nice, but it's unrelated scope and won't be obvious to anyone bisecting a color regression later. Worth a sentence in the PR description at minimum.

---

## `pkg/providers/antigravitycli/path_utils.go`

**Lines 13-32: Path constants**

- (14) ✅ The comment explaining that `~/.gemini/` is shared with the Gemini CLI provider but the subtrees never overlap is genuinely valuable — that's the first question a reviewer asks.
- (15) ✅ `transcriptFileName` vs `fallbackTranscriptFileName` with the double-encoding rationale documented at the constant is the right place for it.

**Lines 86-107: `resolveTranscriptPath`**

- (16) ⚠️ The `if err == nil { … } else if !os.IsNotExist(err) { … }` shape is repeated verbatim for primary and fallback. A tiny `firstExisting(paths ...string) (string, error)` helper would halve it and read better.
- (17) ✅ Returning `("", nil)` for "no transcript" rather than an error is the right call and is documented.

**Lines 163-165: `findTranscriptByID`**

- (18) ⚠️ This is a one-line pass-through to `resolveTranscriptPath` with no added behavior. It exists only to give `provider.go` a differently-named call. Either inline it or drop it — as-is it's an indirection a reader has to chase.

**Lines 169-200: `canonicalizePath` / `pathWithin`**

- (19) ⚠️ `canonicalizePath` is byte-for-byte the same function as `deepseektui/path_utils.go:184` (and near-identical to `droidcli/provider.go:383`). This PR makes it the third copy. See improvement #4.
- (20) ✅ `pathWithin`'s `rel != ".." && !strings.HasPrefix(rel, "../")` check is the correct way to do this (avoids the classic `/foo` matching `/foobar` string-prefix bug).

---

## `pkg/providers/antigravitycli/transcript_parser.go`

**Lines 18-44: Step source/type constants**

- (21) ✅ Strong comments. The `typeCheckpoint` comment quoting the actual on-disk text (`"{{ CHECKPOINT N }} The earlier parts…"`) is exactly what a future maintainer needs.

**Lines 103-110: `isToolResultStep`**

- (22) ✅ Excellent design decision, well justified: identifying results by *exclusion* rather than an allowlist means new Antigravity result types (SEARCH_WEB, GENERATE_IMAGE…) aren't silently dropped. The comment explains the why, not the how.

**Lines 117-155: `loadHistoryIndex`**

- (23) ✅ The note that the first prompt of a session has an empty `conversationId` (assigned only after turn 1) is a real reverse-engineered gotcha worth documenting.
- (24) ✅ Missing file → empty map + nil error is the right contract for an optional index.

**Lines 161-222: `parseTranscript`**

- (25) ✅ Line 170's `fromFallback := strings.HasSuffix(...)` gating the double-decode is correct and minimal.
- (26) ✅ Lines 192-199: the `sort.SliceStable` by `step_index` with the comment about async results flushing out of file order is the single most important correctness decision in the parser, and it's well explained.
- (27) ⚠️ `session.CreatedAt`/`UpdatedAt` are taken from `steps[0]`/`steps[len-1]` *after* the step_index sort. That's right for `CreatedAt`, but `UpdatedAt` now means "created_at of the highest-indexed step", which for a session ending in an async result may be earlier than the wall-clock last write. Minor, but the field name promises something slightly different than it delivers.
- (28) ⚠️ `loadTaskOutputs` failure is debug-logged but the `TaskOutputs` map is left nil — fine, since map reads on nil are safe. Worth noting only because the guard clause structure (`if err == nil { … } else { … }`) reads backwards; `if err != nil { log; } else { assign }` matches the codebase's guard-clause style better.

**Lines 227-260: `loadTaskOutputs`**

- (29) ✅ `filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(transcriptPath))` to reach `.system_generated/` is correct but slightly opaque. The doc comment saves it.
- (30) ⚠️ Three `continue`-on-error branches silently swallow `os.ReadFile` failures with no log at all (line 252). One `slog.Debug` would make a permissions problem diagnosable.

**Lines 266-285: `normalizeFallbackArgs`**

- (31) ✅ Correct handling: only strings are re-decoded, undecodable values pass through. Comment gives concrete examples (`"false"`→bool). Good.

**Lines 290-322: `sessionMetadata`**

- (32) ✅ The comment explaining *why* the summaries DB is preferred but can't be relied on (async, partial) is exactly right.

**Lines 326-336: `firstUserPromptText`**

- (33) ⚠️ Inconsistency: this accepts *any* `USER_INPUT` step, but `buildExchanges` (agent_session.go:148) only accepts `USER_INPUT` **with** `Source == USER_EXPLICIT`. A session whose only user step has a different source would produce valid metadata/slug but then fail conversion with "no conversational exchanges". Either both should filter on source or neither should.

## `pkg/providers/antigravitycli/agent_session.go`

**Lines 33-53: Regexes and path-key lists**

- (34) ✅ `modelRe`'s comment explaining the terminator choice (period-then-whitespace, so `3.5` isn't truncated) is great — and it's backed by a test.
- (35) ⚠️ `toolPathArgKeys` is exactly `workspaceDirArgKeys ∪ workspaceFileArgKeys`. Deriving it (or documenting that it must stay the union) would prevent the three lists drifting apart.
- (36) ⚠️ **DRY**: `markdown_tools.go:331-336` declares a *fourth* list of the same PascalCase path keys (`"AbsolutePath", "TargetFile", "Cwd", "DirectoryPath", "SearchPath"`) for path hints. Adding a new Antigravity path arg now requires edits in two files that don't reference each other.

**Lines 136-197: `buildExchanges`**

- (37) 🔴 **Stale/contradictory comment.** Line 132-133 says: *"Steps are processed in file order (NOT by step_index — the index has a benign gap at 4)"*. But `parseTranscript` now sorts `session.Steps` by `step_index` before this ever runs (line 197), and `provider_test.go:292` exists specifically to prove that sorting is required. The comment describes the pre-fix behavior and will actively mislead the next maintainer into "fixing" the sort.
- (38) ✅ The `flush` closure + `current` pointer is a clean, readable way to express turn grouping.
- (39) ⚠️ The `switch` at line 147 uses `switch { case cond: }` with a mix of type checks and `isToolResultStep`. A `USER_INPUT` step with a non-`USER_EXPLICIT` source falls through to `default:` and gets logged as "unrecognized step" — which is misleading, since it *is* recognized, just intentionally skipped.
- (40) ✅ Assigning `ExchangeID` and back-filling empty timestamps in a single post-pass (lines 186-194) is tidier than threading it through the loop.

**Lines 280-321: `attachToolResult` / `pickPendingTool`**

- (41) ✅ This is the cleverest part of the provider and it's well documented: type-first correlation with FIFO fallback, because Antigravity emits no call→result id. The comment explains the failure mode it prevents (out-of-order completion of concurrent calls).
- (42) ✅ Orphan results are debug-logged rather than silently dropped.
- (43) ⚠️ `strings.EqualFold(step.Status, "RUNNING")` — `"RUNNING"` is a magic string, while every other on-disk enum value in this package got a named const (`typeUserInput`, `sourceUserExplicit`…). The spec documents a full status enum (§3.3); a `statusRunning` const would match the file's own conventions.

**Lines 348-379: `resultBoilerplate` / `cleanResultContent`**

- (44) ✅ The comment justifying substring (not line) matching — because agy appends boilerplate inline after real content — prevents someone "simplifying" this into a line filter and breaking it.
- (45) ⚠️ The five boilerplate strings are matched exactly; a single wording change in a future `agy` release silently reintroduces them into every rendered session. Not fixable in general, but it's the most version-fragile code here and deserves a note pointing at the `agy` version it was verified against (the spec says 1.0.2/1.1.x).

**Lines 435-480: workspace resolution & matching**

- (46) 🔴 **The inferred workspace can be far too broad, and it leaks sessions across projects.** `resolveSessionWorkspace` falls back to `commonPathPrefix` of every path a tool touched. If a print-mode session reads one file in `$HOME` and one in a project, the common prefix is `$HOME` — and `sessionMatchesProject` (line 470) accepts a match in *either* nesting direction, so that session then matches every project under the home directory. I verified this against the real code:

  ```
  paths: /Users/sean/.zshrc + /Users/sean/Source/projA/main.go
  inferred workspace = "/Users/sean"
  matches /Users/sean/Source/projB      = true   ← wrong project
  matches /Users/sean/Documents/notes   = true   ← wrong project
  ```
  This is precisely the pollution the PR description says unscoped sessions were designed to avoid; the guard just doesn't cover the *shallow-inference* case. The `len(common) <= 1` check at line 570 only rejects a literal `/`. Options: require the inferred dir to contain a project marker (`.git`), reject inferred prefixes at or above `$HOME`, or — simplest — only allow the `pathWithin(session.Workspace, projectPath)` direction when the workspace was *inferred* rather than read from history/config.
- (47) ✅ `sessionWorkspaceKnown` and its use in `GetAgentChatSession` (provider.go:163) is a genuinely thoughtful piece of design, and the comment explains the tradeoff clearly.
- (48) ⚠️ `collectToolPaths` and `collectWorkspacePaths` are ~85% the same loop. One function taking a "reduce files to their parent dir" flag would remove the near-duplicate.
- (49) ⚠️ `commonPathPrefix`'s doc says "the deepest **directory** that is an ancestor of every given path", but for a single input it returns that input unchanged — which may be a file. It happens to be safe because `collectWorkspacePaths` pre-dirs file args, but the contract as written doesn't hold (and the test at `agent_session_test.go:286` enshrines the file-returning behavior).

**Lines 578-591: `stripFileURI`**

- (50) ✅ Correct handling of percent-escapes; tested with a spaced path.
- (51) ⚠️ It lives in `agent_session.go` but is used by `project_mapping.go` and `markdown_tools.go` too. `path_utils.go` is the file its name says it belongs in.

**Lines 604-619: `writeDebugRaw`**

- (52) ✅ Matches the sibling providers' debug-raw contract, and the comment noting session-data.json is written centrally prevents duplicate-output confusion.

**Lines 24-34: Log-scraping regexes**

- (72) 🔴 **No doc comment anywhere on the regex block.** These five patterns encode assumptions about `agy`'s *internal log format* — arguably the most fragile dependency in the whole provider — and there's nothing saying which `agy` version they were derived from, that this is a best-effort heuristic, or what breaks when Google changes a log line. The comment says *"WAL mode keeps reads from blocking a live agy writer"* — which the statement can't actually deliver here. (`cursorcli/sqlite_reader.go:185-199` has the identical pattern, so this is copied convention, not a new invention — but the comment overstates it in both places.)   } else {

# The 5 most important improvements

**A. Fix the over-broad workspace inference (observation 46) — this is the only correctness bug I'd block on.**
A print-mode session that touches any file outside the project infers a shallow common ancestor (verified: `$HOME`), and because `sessionMatchesProject` accepts nesting in either direction, that session then attaches to *every* project underneath it. The unscoped-session guard was built for exactly this pollution but doesn't cover the inference case. Cheapest correct fix: track whether the workspace was *inferred* vs *authoritative* (history/config), and for inferred workspaces only accept `pathWithin(workspace, projectPath)` — not the reverse. A `.git` marker check or an "at or above `$HOME` is not a workspace" rule would also work.

**B. Stop discarding index-load errors (observation 102).**
Eight sites do `history, _ := loadHistoryIndex()`. These indexes drive workspace resolution — when they fail, sync silently returns nothing for the project and there's no diagnostic at any log level. Add `slog.Debug` at each site, or wrap both loads in one `loadIndexes()` helper that logs once and returns both.

**C. Fix the stale `buildExchanges` comment (observation 37).**
It says steps are processed "in file order (NOT by step_index)" when `parseTranscript` now explicitly sorts by `step_index`, and a test exists to prove the sort is required. As written it invites someone to remove the sort.

**D. Extract the copy-pasted provider helpers into `pkg/spi` (observations 19, 53, 70, 92, 109).**
`stringValue`, `renderJSONValue`, `normalizeToolName`, `todoSymbol`, `languageFromPath`, `formatDiffBlock`, `renderGenericJSON`, `canonicalizePath`, `dispatchSession`, `classifyCheckError`, `trackCheckSuccess/Failure` are byte-identical across `deepseektui`, `droidcli`, and now `antigravitycli` — roughly 200 duplicated lines. This PR didn't create the pattern, but it's now the third or fourth copy, which is the point where "following existing patterns" and "DRY" genuinely conflict. Worth a follow-up ticket even if not this PR: `pkg/spi/toolrender` + `pkg/spi/checkerror` would let a future provider be ~40% smaller.

**E. Document the log-scraping heuristics in `project_mapping.go` (observations 72, 73, 77, 78).**
Nine of thirteen functions have no doc comment, and the ones missing them are precisely the fragile ones: regexes against `agy`'s internal log lines, the pending-conversation attribution assumption, and treating `project.Name` as a filesystem path. Note the `agy` version these were derived from and state the failure mode when the format changes.

---

# Test assessment

**Overall: strong.** ~70 cases, one test file per source file, real filesystem fixtures via `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` with shared helpers (`writeConversation`, `writeHistory`, `writeProjectConfig`, `writeAntigravityLog`) rather than mocks. Nothing tests the standard library or a third-party package. No flakiness: the only timing-sensitive tests use a polling `waitFor` rather than fixed sleeps.

**The standout: `provider_test.go:292` `TestGetAgentChatSession_ToolResultCorrelation`.** This is the best test in the PR. It writes steps in deliberately *scrambled file order* and its comment enumerates the three distinct bugs it catches — orphaned async results without step_index sorting, FIFO-swapped results without type-aware routing, and dropped `SEARCH_WEB` results with a hardcoded allowlist. Each assertion maps to a specific decision in the code. That's precisely the "complicated logic and combinatorial scenarios" the project's testing strategy calls for.

Also genuinely valuable: `TestBuildExchanges_SkipsCheckpoint` (asserts the content doesn't leak, not just the count), `TestProcessTranscriptFile_PrefersPrimaryForFallbackEvents` (distinguishes the two transcripts by content, so it actually proves preference), `TestAttachToolResult_FIFOAndOrphan` (verifies the orphan doesn't *overwrite* a resolved tool — a real bug class), `TestNormalizeFallbackArgs` (type-asserts bool/float64, not just string equality), and `TestListAgentChatSessions_PrefersSummaryName` (three-way title/preview/fallback matrix).

### Tests I'd change

- (118) ⚠️ **`TestMsEpochToRFC3339` (transcript_parser_test.go:150) is half-tautological.** `msEpochToRFC3339(1779831073907) == ""` only proves the function returned *something*. Assert the exact string (`"2026-05-25T…Z"`) — otherwise a timezone or format regression passes.
- (119) ⚠️ **`TestExpandTilde` (antigravity_exec_test.go:43) asserts `got != "~/bin/agy"`.** That passes for any wrong expansion. Assert equality with `filepath.Join(home, "bin/agy")`.
- (120) ⚠️ **`TestRenderInputs` and `TestRenderHighValueInputs` are sequential `if` blocks, not table-driven.** Seven independent renderers tested as one function means a failure in the first doesn't stop the rest but the failure message doesn't identify the case, and adding an eighth renderer means appending another bespoke block. These are the clearest candidates for `[]struct{name string; render func() string; wantContains, wantAbsent []string}`. Same for `TestClassifyCheckError` (three sequential ifs) and `TestResolveSessionWorkspace` (three sequential scenarios, each with its own error message).
- (121) ⚠️ **`TestProcessTranscriptFile_IgnoresTranscriptOutsideBrain` uses a fixed `time.Sleep(25ms)` then asserts `calls == 0`.** It can never fail spuriously, but it can *pass* spuriously — if the code regressed and the callback fired at 30ms, the test would still be green. Not flaky, just weaker than it looks. Reusing the polling approach inverted (poll for 100ms, fail if the counter ever moves) would be honest.
- (122) ⚠️ **`TestDeriveSlug` asserts `got != "" && got != fallbackSlug`** rather than the actual expected slug. It would pass if the slug generator returned garbage.

### Tests I'd add

- (123) **Workspace-inference breadth (improvement A).** A table-driven test over `resolveSessionWorkspace` + `sessionMatchesProject`: paths spanning `$HOME`, paths under one project, paths split across two projects. This is the case where the current behavior is wrong, and the existing `TestCommonPathPrefix` and `TestSessionMatchesProject` both stop short of it — `TestSessionMatchesProject` sets `Workspace` explicitly rather than exercising the inference path.
- (124) **The unscoped-in-bulk-listing exclusion.** The PR's headline behavioral claim is that text-only sessions "are returned only on explicit `-s <id>` requests, never in project-filtered bulk listings." `TestGetAgentChatSession_UnscopedReturnedByID` tests half of that; the other half — `GetAgentChatSessions(someProject, …)` must *not* include `conv-text` — has no test at all. That's the assertion that protects against project pollution.
- (125) **Timestamps under out-of-order file lines.** `TestGetAgentChatSession_ToolResultCorrelation` proves the sort fixes *correlation*, but `parseTranscript`'s `CreatedAt`/`UpdatedAt` derivation from `steps[0]`/`steps[len-1]` after sorting (observation 27) isn't asserted anywhere with scrambled input.
- (126) **`ensureResumeArgs` with the `--conversation=<id>` form.** Four of the five branches are tested; the `=`-form repair path (`antigravity_exec.go:81-88`) — which uses `slices.Clone` specifically to avoid mutating the caller — is not.
- (127) **`collapseBlankLines` / `cleanResultContent` with tab-indented multi-line RUN_COMMAND output.** `TestCleanResultContent_StripsHeaderAndBoilerplate` covers a diff result; the tab-stripping path is only incidentally covered inside `TestBuildExchanges_GroupsAndAttaches`, and blank-line collapsing after boilerplate removal isn't asserted at all.

**No tests I'd delete** — nothing here is testing Go or a third-party library, and I found no assertion that couldn't fail on a real regression (the four weak ones above are worth strengthening rather than removing).

## The bug

### Where the inferred workspace comes from

`resolveSessionWorkspace` (`pkg/providers/antigravitycli/agent_session.go:440`) tries three sources in order:

1. **`history.jsonl`** — authoritative, written by `agy` itself with the real workspace.
2. **CLI-log → project-config join** — authoritative-ish, scraped from `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/*.log` + `~/.gemini/config/projects/*.json`.
3. **Inference** — `commonPathPrefix(collectWorkspacePaths(steps))`: take every absolute path the session's tools touched (file args reduced to their parent directory), and return the deepest directory that is an ancestor of all of them.

Source 3 only runs when 1 and 2 both miss. That happens for **`agy -p` print-mode sessions** (Antigravity doesn't log those to `history.jsonl` at all — documented in the PR description and the format spec §5.1), and for any session whose CLI logs have rotated away.

### Why the inference goes wrong

`commonPathPrefix` (`agent_session.go:547`) has exactly one floor: it returns `""` when the paths disagree at the *first* segment. In practice that only rejects a literal `/`. Anything else is accepted, however shallow.

So a print-mode session that reads `~/.gitconfig` and then works in a repo produces:

```
/Users/sean/.zshrc                    → /Users/sean
/Users/sean/Source/projA/main.go      → /Users/sean/Source/projA
common ancestor                       → /Users/sean
```

The workspace is now the home directory. One stray path outside the repo — a `Cwd` of `$HOME`, reading a dotfile, `run_command` in `/tmp` — is enough.

### Why that leaks across projects

`sessionMatchesProject` (`agent_session.go:465`) accepts a match in **either** nesting direction:

```go
if pathWithin(session.Workspace, projectPath) || pathWithin(projectPath, session.Workspace) {
```

The second direction exists for a good reason: if `history.jsonl` records a monorepo root and you run `specstory sync` from a subdirectory, the session should still match. But with `Workspace == "/Users/sean"`, *every* project under the home directory is "inside the workspace". I ran this against the real code:

```
inferred workspace                    = "/Users/sean"
matches /Users/sean/Source/projB      = true   ← never touched projB
matches /Users/sean/Documents/notes   = true   ← never touched it either
```

### Impact

Three user-visible consequences, all for print-mode sessions only:

1. **`specstory sync antigravity` in projB writes projA's conversation into projB's `.specstory/history/`** — and syncs it to the cloud tagged to projB. Cross-project contamination in the artifact users actually read.
2. **`DetectAgent` returns true for projects with no Antigravity activity**, so the CLI reports the agent as active everywhere.
3. **`ListAllAgentChatSessions` hands `OriginCwd = "/Users/sean"` to `specstory reindex`**, which maps the session to a bogus home-directory "project" in the session index.

Note this is precisely the pollution the PR already defends against elsewhere — `sessionWorkspaceKnown` + the by-id-only rule for unscoped sessions (`provider.go:163`) exists to stop text-only sessions from appearing in every project. The guard just doesn't cover the case where inference *succeeds* but produces something far too shallow.

---

## The three fixes

### 1. Provenance + `$HOME` floor

Make `resolveSessionWorkspace` return whether the workspace was authoritative or inferred, and store that on `agSession`. Then:

- **Matching:** authoritative workspaces keep both directions. Inferred workspaces only match *downward* — the workspace must be inside the project.
- **Inference:** reject a common prefix that is at or above `$HOME`.

True positives survive because `sessionMatchesProject` also scans `collectToolPaths` — any session that touched a file inside the project still matches regardless of what its workspace resolved to. In the example above, projA still matches (it has the tool path), projB no longer does.

**Cost:** ~15 lines, no filesystem access. **Loss:** an inferred workspace that is legitimately a *parent* of the project stops matching by workspace — but for the inference to have produced that ancestor, a tool must have touched something inside the project, so the tool-path scan catches it anyway.

### 2. Provenance only

Same directional rule, no floor on inference.

Fixes the matching (consequences 1 and 2 above), but the session's workspace *value* is still `/Users/sean`. That value is published in two places: `WorkspaceRoot` in the generated session data, and `OriginCwd` in `ListAllAgentChatSessions`. So consequence 3 — `reindex` creating a home-directory project — remains. It's half the fix for most of the work.

### 3. Require a `.git` marker

Walk from the inferred candidate looking for a `.git` entry; use that directory, or give up.

The most precise notion of "project root", and it would actually *improve* inference quality in the good case (a session confined to `projA/pkg/` would resolve up to `projA` rather than staying at `pkg`).

But: it costs `os.Stat` calls per session on the sync hot path; it silently drops any project directory that isn't a git repo (workspace becomes `""`, so the session goes unscoped and disappears from bulk listings); and **it doesn't fix the directional problem on its own** — a git-verified monorepo root above the project still matches every sibling package under the bidirectional rule. You'd want fix 1's matching rule regardless.

---

## Recommendation

**Fix 1.** It addresses both halves of the problem — how sessions are matched *and* what workspace value gets published to the session data and the reindexer — with no filesystem I/O and no loss of true positives, since the tool-path scan already covers the cases the stricter workspace rule gives up. Fix 3 is a genuine improvement to inference *quality* rather than *safety*, and is better as a follow-up once there's real-world data on how often print-mode sessions matter; layering it on later is additive and doesn't invalidate fix 1.

Which would you like?

// ValidateSessionData runs schema validation on SessionData when in debug mode.
// Validation is only performed when debugRaw is true to avoid overhead in normal operation.
// Returns true if validation passed or was skipped, false if validation failed.
func ValidateSessionData(session *spi.AgentChatSession, debugRaw bool) bool {
	if !debugRaw || session.SessionData == nil {
		return true
	}
	if !session.SessionData.Validate() {
		slog.Warn("SessionData failed schema validation, proceeding anyway",
			"sessionId", session.SessionID)
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// WriteDebugSessionData writes debug session data when debugRaw is enabled.
// Logs warnings on failure but does not fail the operation.
func WriteDebugSessionData(session *spi.AgentChatSession, debugRaw bool) {
	if !debugRaw || session.SessionData == nil {
		return
	}
	if err := spi.WriteDebugSessionData(session.SessionID, session.SessionData); err != nil {
		slog.Warn("Failed to write debug session data", "sessionId", session.SessionID, "error", err)
	}
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-07-24 19:37:45Z)**_

You're right, and I can show it. Dropping inference costs almost nothing, because `sessionMatchesProject` already falls through to a scan of every path the tools touched:

```
Workspace = "" (inference removed), session read ~/.zshrc + /Users/sean/Source/projA/main.go

matches projA (its real project) = true    ← via tool-path scan, unchanged
matches projB (unrelated)        = false   ← the bug, gone
WorkspaceRoot when synced from projA = "/Users/sean/Source/projA"   ← was "/Users/sean"
```

So print-mode sessions are still captured in the project they belong to; they just stop claiming a workspace they can't actually prove. What's lost:

- **`OriginCwd` is empty for print-mode sessions in `reindex`** — they get enumerated globally but stay unmapped to a project. That's the same bucket the PR already puts text-only sessions in (`TestListAllAgentChatSessions` asserts exactly that for `conv-2`), so it's consistent rather than a new gap.
- **`WorkspaceRoot` can be `""`** when `GetAgentChatSession` is called with an empty cwd. 354	### 5.3 Recommended workspace-inference strategy for the parser
355	In priority order:
356	1. **history.jsonl `workspace`** keyed by matching `conversationId` — authoritative
357	   when present (interactive sessions only).
358	2. **CLI-log/config join** — map `conversationId -> projectId` from retained
359	   `antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log`, then `projectId -> workspace` from
360	   `config/projects/*.json`.
361	3. **Tool-arg paths in the transcript** — derive the workspace from the most
362	   common ancestor of `Cwd` (run_command), `AbsolutePath` (view_file),
363	   `TargetFile` (write/edit), `SearchPath` (grep_search), `DirectoryPath`
364	   (list_dir). For print-mode `--add-dir` sessions these are absolute and
365	   consistently point at the workspace.
366	4. If none resolve (e.g. the no-`--add-dir` session that wandered the whole
367	   filesystem), mark workspace **unknown** — do not guess. Note: `agy -p` with no
368	   `--add-dir` defaults the workspace to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch`

All 18 items are addressed. `gofmt` clean, `go build ./...` and the full `go test ./...` pass, `golangci-lint run` reports 0 issues.

## What changed

**A — workspace inference removed** (`agent_session.go`, `transcript_parser.go`)

Per your call, `resolveSessionWorkspace` now only returns workspaces Antigravity states itself (history.jsonl, then the CLI-log/project-config join) and returns `""` otherwise. `commonPathPrefix` and `collectWorkspacePaths` are deleted. Verified end-to-end against the original repro:

```
sync from projA (real)      -> 1 session, DetectAgent=true
sync from projB (unrelated) -> 0 sessions, DetectAgent=false   (was 1 leaked session)
global ref OriginCwd=""                                        (was "/Users/sean")
```

`$HOME` still matches that session, correctly — it genuinely read `~/.zshrc`, and the tool-path scan requires a path actually inside the candidate project.

**B — index errors logged** (`transcript_parser.go`, `provider.go`, `watcher.go`)

`loadWorkspaceIndexes()` and `loadSummaries()` replace all eight `x, _ :=` sites, each logging at debug what degrades when the load fails.

**C/37, 39, 43** — the `buildExchanges` comment now describes the step_index ordering that actually happens; non-explicit `USER_INPUT` gets its own branch instead of being logged as "unrecognized"; `"RUNNING"` is now `statusRunning` alongside the other on-disk enum constants.

**103, 104, 108** — `DetectAgent` answers from the indexes first and only parses transcripts for conversations with no stated workspace; `GetAgentChatSessions` calls `progress` exactly once per file via a new `convertConversation` helper; the doc pointer now cites `docs/antigravity-format-spec.md §1.1`.

**91, 87, 85** — both watcher paths funnel through one `emitConversation`; `processTranscriptFile` uses guard clauses and logs the stat failure it used to swallow; `watchState.watchedDirs` makes re-scans cost one `ReadDir` instead of an `fsnotify.Add` per conversation, with Remove/Rename events untracking so a recreated directory is re-watched.

**72, 77, 80** — the log-scraping regexes carry a block comment stating they match agy 1.0.2–1.1.x, that they're best-effort, and how a silent format change manifests; the `project.Name`-as-path fallback explains that CLI-created projects store the path there; `return scanner.Err()`.

**8, 9, 18, 35, 36** — the agent column width is computed once into `m.agentColW` with a named `agentColMinWidth` replacing the four magic `8`s; `findTranscriptByID` is gone; `toolPathArgKeys` is the single canonical path-key list that `markdown_tools.go` now builds from.

## Tests

Replaced `TestCommonPathPrefix` and `TestResolveSessionWorkspace_SingleFileUsesParent` (both tested deleted code). `TestResolveSessionWorkspace` is now table-driven with four cases including the deliberate no-guess one. Added `TestSessionMatchesProject_NoStatedWorkspace` (the regression guard — a print-mode session reaches its own project and not a sibling) and `TestWorkspacesOverlap`.

One thing worth knowing: my first draft of the regression test failed because `t.TempDir()` is a symlink on macOS and `pathWithin` canonicalizes both sides, so a *non-existent* file can't resolve into its project directory. The fixture now writes real files. Production paths always exist, so this is a test-fixture constraint rather than a code defect — but it's a trap for anyone writing path tests in this package.

## Needs your attention

Two things I couldn't change from here:

1. **The PR description** still says the workspace is "inferred from the absolute paths the tools touched" — that's now wrong. I updated §5.3 and §11 of the format spec to document the decision and why inference was rejected.
2. **Item 13 from the review** — the palette rebrand for claude/codex/gemini/droid/deepseek in `colorForAgent` is still unrelated scope riding along in this PR. Not in your list, so I left it, but it's worth a line in the description.

373	**Google Antigravity** is a dedicated, agentic software development platform released by Google to support developers in an era of AI-driven workflows[1][2][3]. It is designed to function as an "agent-first" ecosystem, moving beyond traditional code completion tools to allow autonomous AI agents to plan, execute, and verify complex tasks across an editor, terminal, and browser[4][2][5].
374	
375	### Key Components of the Antigravity Ecosystem
376	The platform has evolved into a comprehensive suite of tools[6][7]:
377	*   **Antigravity (Standalone App):** The flagship application for Windows, macOS, and Linux, serving as a "command center" to launch, monitor, and orchestrate multiple local AI agents in parallel[6][8].
378	*   **Antigravity IDE:** A specialized, AI-powered IDE (often described as a heavily modified fork of VS Code) that includes deep codebase understanding, an agent manager, and artifact tracking[6][9].
379	*   **Antigravity CLI:** A command-line interface for terminal-based agent interactions[6][9].
380	*   **Antigravity SDK:** Tools that allow developers to programmatically integrate Antigravity agents into their own custom systems[6][10].
381	
382	### Core Features
383	*   **Agentic Autonomy:** Instead of just suggesting snippets of code, agents can be delegated end-to-end tasks, such as implementing new features, running tests, or performing code reviews, with the ability to operate across different development surfaces[2][11].
384	*   **Multi-Model Support:** The platform supports various AI models, including Google’s Gemini 3 series, Anthropic’s Claude models, and open-source variants[9][3].
385	*   **Artifacts:** To build trust, agents generate "Artifacts"—tangible deliverables like implementation plans, task lists, and recordings—that allow you to verify the agent's work at a glance[11].
386	*   **Asynchronous Workflow:** It enables developers to offload long-running tasks to the background, allowing them to focus on other work while the agent progresses[11].
387

391	If you encountered the term "antigravity" in the context of the **Python programming language**, it refers to a famous **Easter egg**[12][13]. In Python, typing `import antigravity` into your code or terminal does not trigger an AI coding assistant; instead, it automatically opens your web browser to a classic [xkcd comic (#353)](https://xkcd.com/353/) about Python[14][15][16]. This is a long-standing joke in the Python community and is unrelated to Google's AI development platform[13].

## What went

**19 fabricated tool names** dropped from `classifyToolType`: `create_file`, `edit_file`, `apply_patch`, `read_file`, `read_directory`, `codebase_search`, `file_search`, `find_files`, `web_search`, `read_url`, `fetch_url`, `execute_url`, `run_terminal_command`, `exec`, `shell`, `update_plan`, `todo_write`, `create_plan`, `task_list`. The five per-call `map[string]bool` allocations went with them — it's now a plain switch over the real names.

**Three renderer functions** deleted, since every name that reached them was invented: `renderFileSearchInput` (`codebase_search`/`file_search`/`find_files`), `renderApplyPatch` (`apply_patch`), `renderTodoWrite` (`update_plan`/`todo_write`/`create_plan`), plus `todoSymbol`, which only `renderTodoWrite` used.

**Alias cases** collapsed in `formatToolInput` — `"runcommand"` no longer also answers to `exec`/`shell`/`runterminalcommand`, `"viewfile"` no longer to `readfile`, and so on.

I left the *argument-key* fallbacks alone (`stringValue(args, "Query", "pattern", "query", ...)`). Antigravity is genuinely inconsistent about casing — `search_web` uses lowercase `query` while `read_url_content` uses PascalCase `Url` — so those lists are cheap insurance on real tools, not guesses about which tools exist.

`ask_permission` is the one real tool with no renderer. Its argument shape has never been captured, so it falls through to the raw-argument fallback rather than getting a layout I'd have to invent — same principle as the removals.

## Verification

Re-rendered the captured session end-to-end against the live binary. All 18 exercised tools still render, and the full output is **byte-identical** to the committed markdown. Full `go test ./...` passes, `golangci-lint run` at 0 issues.

Two side effects worth noting. First, `-s <id>` from the wrong directory correctly returned nothing — that session's workspace is the multi-agent project, so the by-id guard excluded it until I ran from there. Unplanned confirmation that the guard works. Second, `TestClassifyToolType` is now the full 19-tool table plus an unknown, so it serves as the in-repo record of which names exist — the comment says a name absent from it shouldn't be special-cased anywhere in the provider.

I also rewrote spec §3.5 with the authoritative list and an explicit note that `codebase_search`, `execute_url`, `read_url`, `apply_patch`, `todo_write`, `update_plan` and the rest were guesses that got implemented and removed — so the next maintainer doesn't re-add them from the old text.
